title: Beyond SMART Goals: The STELLAR Framework for Values-Aligned and Sustainable Goal Pursuit—STELLAR Framework
content: Goal setting is central to human self-regulation, yet technically well-specified goals do not necessarily produce sustained goal pursuit. The widely used SMART heuristic offers a practical structure for formulating objectives, but its principal emphasis is on properties of the stated goal rather than on the broader fit among the goal, the person pursuing it, available resources, and changing circumstances. This conceptual article introduces STELLAR, a seven-component framework for designing goals that are not only sufficiently structured and clearly targeted but also personally coherent, resource-compatible, manageable, adaptable, and feasible. STELLAR comprises Structured, Targeted, Energizing, Logical, Light, Adaptive, and Realistic dimensions. Structured and Targeted provide route coherence and evaluable direction; Energizing concerns compatibility between pursuit demands and sustainable resources; Logical captures coherence with personal values, needs, identity, and life direction; Light concerns manageable proximal action; Adaptive enables revision of strategies or pathways as circumstances change; and Realistic addresses feasibility relative to the individual’s current starting position and constraints. The framework integrates goal-setting theory, goal-systems research, self-concordance, self-determination theory, self-efficacy, implementation intentions, subgoal research, progress monitoring, resource allocation, and adaptive goal regulation. Seventeen testable propositions are developed, including a component-matched goal-redesign proposition. The article positions STELLAR as an extension of goal specification toward multidimensional goal-pursuit design and outlines a program for psychometric, longitudinal, experimental, comparative, and intervention-based validation.
